topic: The Magic of Space-Filling Curves: How Lines Fill Planes

sections.title: The Paradox: Can a Line Fill a Square?
lecture_lines: Can a one-dimensional line fill a square?
Imagine a snake getting thinner and longer.
It eventually blankets the entire surface area.
animations: 1. Create a unit square centered on screen (#FFFFFF).
2. Display a single line segment across the square (#FF0000).
3. Transform segment into a wavy path filling the space (#00FF00).

sections.title: The Peano Curve Construction (The Iterative Process)
lecture_lines: We create these via an iterative process.
Divide the line into smaller segments.
Replace segments with a recursive folding pattern.
animations: 1. Define a 3x3 grid inside the unit square (#FFFFFF).
2. Draw a path connecting grid centers (#FF0000).
3. Subdivide grid and refine the path recursively (#00FF00).

sections.title: The Hilbert Curve: Efficiency in Data Mapping
lecture_lines: The Hilbert curve is highly efficient.
It preserves locality between nearby points.
Think of a robot cleaning a room.
It never crosses its own track.
Total travel distance is minimized here.
animations: 1. Present a 2x2 grid representing data space (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Real-World Applications: From GPS to Image Processing
lecture_lines: These curves optimize spatial database indexing.
They also improve memory cache locality.
Fractal antennas fit into tiny devices.
They maintain excellent signal strength throughout.
Spatial mapping is everywhere in technology.
animations: 2. Use Hilbert curve to index locations (#FF0000).
3. Demonstrate rapid lookup in indexed space (#00FF00).

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Intuition
lecture_lines: We see folded origami patterns appearing.
Geometry reveals the hidden filling logic.
animations: 1. Reveal unit square filled with curve (#FFFFFF).
2. Highlight the density of the curve (#FF0000).
3. Final fading of lines to reveal full coverage (#00FF00).
